name: New User Onboarding
primary_user_goal: Download Arc and learn its unique interface paradigm
business_goal: Convert website visitors into active Arc users and guide them through the learning curve
exit_point: Completed setup with at least one Space configured
description: Arc's onboarding is critical because it asks users to unlearn decades of browser muscle memory. The flow balances excitement about new possibilities with gentle tutorials for unfamiliar concepts like vertical tabs and Spaces.
friction_points: Paradigm shift from horizontal to vertical tabs
Understanding pinned vs today's tabs distinction
success_metrics: Creation of second Space within first week

name: Daily Browsing Workflow
primary_user_goal: Browse the web efficiently with minimal tab chaos
business_goal: Prove Arc's productivity benefits through daily usage superiority
entry_point: Opening Arc or clicking external link
exit_point: Closing Arc or switching to another app
description: The core browsing flow demonstrates Arc's reimagined approach to everyday web use. Users navigate primarily through the Command Bar, manage tabs in the sidebar, and handle quick lookups through Little Arc without cluttering their workspace.
friction_points: Muscle memory for traditional browser shortcuts
success_metrics: Average tabs open (should decrease over time)
Little Arc vs full tab ratio for external links

name: Context Switching with Spaces
primary_user_goal: Maintain separate browsing contexts for different life areas
business_goal: Create switching costs that increase Arc loyalty and demonstrate unique value
entry_point: Creating a new Space or switching between existing Spaces
exit_point: Settled into appropriate Space for current task
description: Spaces enable users to maintain completely separate browsing contexts. A user might have Work, Personal, and Side Project spaces, each with different tabs, pinned items, and even different browser profiles for login separation.
key_moments: Customizing Space with color and icon
Realizing tabs don't mix between Spaces

name: Split View Multitasking
primary_user_goal: Work with multiple pages simultaneously without window management
business_goal: Position Arc as essential for knowledge work and productivity
entry_point: Need to view two pages side-by-side
description: Split View allows users to view multiple web pages side-by-side within a single Arc window. Users can drag tabs to create splits, resize panels, and link tabs together for persistent split arrangements.

name: Command Bar Navigation
primary_user_goal: Quickly find and navigate to content without mouse interaction
business_goal: Train users on keyboard-centric workflow that increases efficiency and Arc loyalty
entry_point: Pressing Cmd+T or clicking URL area
exit_point: Navigating to destination or dismissing bar
description: The Command Bar unifies URL entry, tab switching, history search, bookmark access, and Arc actions into a single keyboard-driven interface. It's the primary way power users interact with Arc.
key_moments: Using fuzzy matching for fast access
Finding Arc actions in Command Bar
friction_points: Expectation of separate URL bar and tab search
Learning that Cmd+T does more than new tab

name: Little Arc Quick Lookup
primary_user_goal: Look something up quickly without adding to tab clutter
business_goal: Demonstrate Arc's thoughtful approach to tab management and hygiene
entry_point: Clicking external link or invoking Little Arc manually
exit_point: Closing Little Arc or promoting to full tab
description: Little Arc provides a minimal popup browser for ephemeral tasks. When clicking links from other apps, Little Arc opens instead of creating a new tab. Users can promote important content to full tabs or dismiss after quick lookup.
key_moments: First external link opening in Little Arc
Realizing it didn't create a permanent tab
Promoting content to full tab when needed
friction_points: Initial confusion about popup vs new tab
Wanting external links to always open as tabs
success_metrics: Little Arc sessions vs promotions to tabs

name: Easel Content Capture and Organization
primary_user_goal: Capture, annotate, and organize web research visually
business_goal: Expand Arc's value proposition into knowledge management
entry_point: Creating new Easel or capturing content to existing Easel
exit_point: Completed visual organization or shared Easel
description: Easels provide infinite canvas spaces for visual organization of web content. Users can capture live screenshots, add notes, draw connections, and share their visual research with others.
friction_points: Understanding when Easels are useful vs overkill

name: Boost Website Customization
primary_user_goal: Fix or improve a website's appearance and usability
business_goal: Increase user investment and community engagement through personalization
entry_point: Wanting to change a website's appearance
description: Boosts allow users to customize any website's appearance without technical knowledge. From simple color changes to hiding elements to full CSS overrides, Boosts persist and can be shared with the Arc community.

name: Settings and Preferences Configuration
primary_user_goal: Configure Arc to match personal workflow and preferences
business_goal: Enable power user customization while maintaining approachability
entry_point: Opening Settings via menu or keyboard shortcut
description: Arc's settings balance power and simplicity, offering deep customization while keeping defaults sensible. Settings include keyboard shortcuts, AI features (Arc Max), profile management, and advanced browser configurations.
